propositions: A git fetch to an unresponsive remote (accepts connection, sends zero bytes) hangs until the 300s wall-clock timeout instead of aborting on throughput starvation.
The git subprocess invocation in _fetch_origin lacks http.lowSpeedLimit and http.lowSpeedTime config, leaving no throughput-keyed abort mechanism.
A stalled fetch should abort in ~10 seconds via low-speed detection rather than burning 5 minutes, with in-process retry for transient stalls.
A legitimately slow-but-progressing fetch (e.g. 2000 B/s continuous transfer) must not be aborted; the discriminator is throughput floor, not wall time.
repo_snapshot.py at 788/800 LOC has no room for the fix; the git-subprocess cluster must be extracted to a new sibling git_fetch.py module to stay within the 800 LOC cap.
